pages.name: Overview
pages.html:
The one wealth the poor of this city can boast over the privileged is their incentive to serve behind the bayonet.
 {{                August Haardt, Torch & Clarion }}

The Garrison

The Special Police have seized all the evidence of the Smiling Man Murders and the prime suspect, but the Clarion Society is convinced they have conflicting incentives. With the war escalating and enemy ships spotted north of Anchester, the Anchester Military has need of new weapons to match the Dwarven arms of Sous Terreborgue and the might of a Zeshagu Kirin Phalanx.

Episode Summary
Players 3–6, Level 7
Duration ~4 hours
Pacing Player-Led Investigation; Chase; Combat
Scenes 6 (4)
Cast Miss Sharp; Sir Stowe; the Special Police; five horrors
Reward A page of the Pale Journals; the Shadow's Journal; jars of stolen memory
References Doom Counter; Dread Insight; Chase System; Curse System; Mythos stat blocks; residential maps

Timeline

Fifteen years ago. A collector had the Pale Journals stolen from the Temple of Anhur in Sai Abbadon.

Two years ago. Zeshagu warriors stormed down from the mountains, joined Sous Terreborgue, and took Sai Abbadon.

One year ago. Zeshagu's dragons and Sous Terreborgue's warships sealed Anchester, and only blockade-runners slipped through. The collector had the Journals copied, and the pages began to leak out into the city.

Six months ago. The Anchester Special Police, a military body, secretly began an experiment to build super-soldiers from something they had found in one of the stolen Pale Journals.

Three months ago. Bodies of academics began to be found, their skulls opened above the brow. The Watch named no suspect; the wards named him the Smiling Man.

Two months ago. After being exposed to the horrors of the Mythos, the players joined the Clarion Society, a social club dedicated to uncovering the truth about it.

Yesterday. The players rescued Constance Sharp from the Special Police and investigated a Mythos event at the home of Dr. Pemberton, a psychiatrist connected with the Smiling Man murders.

Today. The players plan to infiltrate the Special Police headquarters in the Garrison and seize the evidence before it is moved north to the front lines at Pashendale.

Episode Structure

This  episode  is  an  infiltration,  built  like  a  dungeon  rather  than  a  straight  line.  The  players  are  breaking  into  the  Army-Navy Yard Garrison to reach the evidence the Special Police have seized. Why they want it is theirs to work out; how they reach it is up to them.

They choose a way in first, and they choose an hour. Four routes lead inside: the delivery yard, a back service door, the front gate, or a drainage pipe running from the laundry out to the drains beyond the wall. By day the halls are crowded and easy to blend into;  by  night  they  are  empty,  and simply being there is reason enough to be stopped.

Inside, the upper Garrison is a living, working post full of soldiers, and the players have no business there. This part runs on talk and stealth: rooms full of things to find, people to fool, codes to lift. Nothing here is a fight yet. The pressure is the Doom Counter, which ticks up every time they are noticed.

An elevator and a stair lead down to the quiet, classified floor. One coded door past it opens the part they came for: a morgue, a row of cells, and the sealed lab where a changed soldier guards the evidence. That last room is the fight.

Assume the alarm goes off. When it does, getting out becomes a running fight, guards arriving in twos and threes under a constant threat of being overwhelmed, until the players break clear of the Garrison.

pages.name: The Doom Counter
pages.html:
Start: equal to the party's number of Dread Insights.

Escalating Doom

Mark Escalation
3 The watch grows uneasy; encounters turn harsher.
6 A section is searched; cover gets hard to hold.
9 Alarm sounds; guards hunt in armed pairs.
12 Fully hunted; overwhelming pressure until they break clear.

Manifesting Doom

Cost Doom
1 Mythos Disadvantage
1 Murphy's Law
1 It's Quiet... Too Quiet
1 Light's Out
1 Papers, Please
2 Paper-Thin Disguise
2 Everyone's a Suspect
2 Cut Off
3 Sound the Alarm!
3 Enemy Reinforcements
3 It Woke Up
5 Activate one Dread Ability

CARNIVAL OF
WANDERING WONDERS
Gates open at dusk; children half off.

Doom

Mythos Disadvantage. Impose disadvantage on a single roll, framed as the Mythos pressing in: the hand shakes, the eye slips, the mind stalls.

Murphy's Law. Something mundane fails at the worst moment. A lamp dies, a lockpick snaps, a lantern gutters, a page tears. Cost a resource or a plan, not health.

It's Quiet... Too Quiet. The bustle of the Garrison drops out of the scene. Call a Mythos check, or force a nervy Perception roll as the party strains to hear what changed.

Lights Out. The lights flicker and the dark closes in. Vision drops, a lit torch becomes a tell, and whatever waits in the dark rooms grows bolder.

Papers, Please. A guard picks this exact moment to want a badge and a name. The party must produce the right cover, talk fast, or find a reason to be somewhere else.

Paper-Thin Disguise. A detail of the cover stops working. A rank worn wrong, a face half-known, a story that does not match. Someone starts to look twice.

Everyone's a Suspect. The mood turns and the party draws the eye: a tail, a second look, a muttered word to a superior. Progress stalls until they talk, slip away, or brazen it out.

Cut Off. The way out closes: a door bars, a checkpoint drops, a patrol fills the corridor. The party is stuck where they stand and must deal with the scene, not flee it.

Sound the Alarm! Trip the alarm early. The Garrison knows, the building wakes, and the episode drops straight into Assault Mode without waiting for the Doom to climb.

Enemy Reinforcements. Fresh soldiers arrive mid-scene: another patrol, a squad off the watch, more of whatever the party is already facing.

It Woke Up. A changed man stirs ahead of schedule: a subject in the cells, a body in the morgue, or the sealed-lab guard, roused early and dangerous.

Activate one Dread Ability. Trigger one of the guard's Dread Abilities. The priciest spend, for the worst single moment of the fight.

pages.name: Operations Flow Chart
pages.html:
The Flow Chart maps choices, not rooms. After the briefing, the gear up, and the approach, the party picks one of the four ways in across the top. Every lane drops down and cross-links to its neighbors, so they can switch routes as they go, and all lead down the stairs or the elevator to the sealed basement, then through one coded door to the dark rooms.

Follow the arrows for how the rooms connect, not the order to run them. There is no fixed sequence and no single correct path; let the players set the route and the pace, and let

them backtrack, split up, or double back through a lane they have already used. The Doom Counter climbs as they are noticed, and each mark tightens the Garrison around them. When it tips to alarm, the infiltration is over and the map becomes a running fight back out.

By day the building is crowded: cover is easy and mistakes happen before witnesses.

By night it is near-empty: stealth is easy, but being anywhere off-hours is suspect, and being found raises the alarm. A room notes the hour only when it changes a roll.

pages.name: The Briefing
pages.html:
The Briefing

Any Location. Any Time. ~10 min

There is a section of the Garrison few can access and inside it is a stack of evidence that will damn a generation. Someone with clean hands and a good posting has been gathering papers that describe ancient magics that should be left alone. And those who seek answers often disappear.

You have followed that trail to its door. You have some badges and some false paperwork. You might yet walk safely among those who would shoot you for a spy, and lift the truth out of a fortress before the secret has time to fester. No monster bars your way. Only the whistle, the ledger, the turned key, and the small cold courtesy of men doing their duty.

The players have seen things, dark things that hide in shadows and behave in revolting ways. While up until now, things have been happening to them, now they have a chance to take the initiative.

Whether through the Clarion Society, or through some other contact, give the players the incentive and opptortunity to infiltrate the Army-Navy Yard Garrison in North Ward. Let them purchase or scrounge for resources. Encourage them to question their contacts. The information should be easily available to them.

The party can discover these things with a little bit of legwork.

  • The evidence is in the sealed basement.
  • There are three ways in: the front door, the back door, and the loading dock.
  • If they ask: "Is there another way in?" let them do a skill check to find the fourth way in.
  • Encourage them to come up with a plan to get into the facility.
  • Make sure they have a plan to get out.

Encourage them to review the evidence they alreayd have. There may likely be something they have missed that will help them along the way.

Finally, make sure they tell you what time of day they are planning to execute their plan. The facility behaves differently in day or night.

pages.name: Gear Up
pages.html:
Gear Up

Any Location. Before the Raid. ~20 min

You are not walking into a fortress with your hands empty. There are people who owe you, people who sell what the City will not, and people who ask no questions if the coin is good. Whatever you mean to carry past two hundred men who would shoot you, now is the time to get it. Take care in what you carry. A heavy weapon or a pry bar mark you as surely as a confession. What gets you in is what looks like it belongs.

This is the shopping scene. Keep it short and let the players prepare with intent. Do not turn it into an afternoon of haggling.

Give them real access, and let them tell you where they go for what:

  • Black markets, for the things the Army would never sell them.
  • The Clarion Society, for tools, documents, and specialist kit.
  • Their own contacts, for favors and one-off items.

While they outfit, steer them toward the things this job actually needs:

  • Cover: credentials, a forged requisition, a work detail's kit. Uniforms can also be lifted on site.
  • Tools: concealed weapons, thieves' tools, a hooded lantern, a camera for the evidence, rope, chalk.
  • A way to signal an abort, and a place to fall back to.

Make plain that inside the Garrison, anything obviously a weapon or a break-in tool is a liability until the shooting starts; concealment matters as much as firepower.

Before they move, make them tell you two things: what each of them is carrying, and their plan to get back out.

pages.name: Approach Garrison
pages.html:
Approach Garrison

Army-Navy Yard, North Ward. ~5 min

The Yard is the heart of the Anchester war effort and is guarded by hard men with stern weapons. Barbed wire and blockades funnel you to the checkpoint at the gates. Sandbags protect the soldiers who stand vigilant day and night through the harshest weather. Searchlights on the roof point toward the sky. You have done your leg-work. Your plan is solid. All that is left is to set it in motion.

Orientation, not a challenge. The plan is already made; this is the moment they arrive, read the ground, and commit. No gate to pass yet, and no wrong choice. Keep it brief and hand off to the entrance they picked.

Let them watch the rhythm before they move:

  • Searchlights sweep the sky, not the ground. The walls are watched for dragons, not for men on foot.
  • Patrols keep the wire, but the watch change leaves a soft window. That is the moment to move.
  • Their way in is waiting: the front gate, the back service door, or the loading dock.

If a player asks after another way and has not already found it, let a skill check turn up the fourth: a drainage pipe that runs from the laundry out past the wall.

If they never fixed their hour, fix it now. The Yard is a different place by day than by night, and every scene after this depends on which they chose.

pages.name: Front Door
pages.html:
Front Door

Main Gate. Day/Night. ~15 min

A striped pole bars the road, with a sentry box and a sergeant's standing desk beneath a hard electric lamp. He takes papers, runs a finger down a list, and works the barrier up and down. Past him the entrance hall opens bright and polished, a rack of rifles by the door, the air thick with tobacco and floor wax.

The bold way in, straight through the front under cover. It is a social gate: present a badge or papers, give a plausible errand, and keep calm.

At the gate, the players will find a grizzled sergeant checking papers and purpose. Allow the players to make skill checks to get information and talk their way past the guard.

Skill Checks

An Insight check (Tricky 16) show that the sergeant is testing whether the errand makes sense, not who they are. A party that leans on a believable errand rolls with advantage.

Deception or Persuasion against the sergeant. Tricky 16 with solid cover and a matching errand, Hard 19 with thin cover, Extreme 22 on nerve alone. - Success and they can freely move through the Long Corridores of the Garrison. - Failure +1 Doom, try another way.

A Perception or Deception check (Tricky 16) will allow the players to scan the sergeant's clipboard for a list of expected arrivals. A name lifted from that list grants advantage on futher deception checks.

pages.name: Back Door
pages.html:
Back Door

Service Alley. Day/Night. ~10 min

A service door on the dark side of the base, behind a stack of empty crates and bins of refuse. A sputtering lamp hangs above it.

The quiet way in: one neglected door, no clerk and no queue. It opens on the mail room.

Skill Checks

Thieves' tools (Routine 13) on the old lock. - Success and move into the Mailroom - Failure +1 Doom, try another method.

Daytime Stealth to slip through when a detail props it open (Tricky 16) - Success and move into the Mailroom - Failure +1 Doom and they need to try another method.

Athletics to force it, (Tricky 16). - Success and move into the Mailroom, +1 Doom. - Failure +2 Doom, try another method.

pages.name: Another Way In
pages.html:
Another Way In

Drainage Outfall. Day/Night. ~5-10 min

Beyond the wall, in a weedy ditch, a pipe empties into a storm drain from the the laundry, tall enough to walk stooped, and the air off it is warm, wet, and faintly of lye. An old iron lock secures a grate across its mouth.

The hidden way in: a drainage pipe from the laundry that runs out under the wall, past every gate. Get the grate off and sneak up the pipe.

Skill Checks

Athletics (Tricky 16) to pull the grate loose, or Thieves' tools (Tricky 16) on the lock. - Success and they pull the grate and crawl the pipe up into the Laundry. - Failure +2 Doom and the grate gives with a screech.

pages.name: Deliveries
pages.html:
Deliveries

Delivery Yard. Day/Night. ~10-15 min

Wagons and steam lorries queue at a wire gate, engines ticking, horses stamping in the cold. A clerk leans from a booth with a clipboard, stamping manifests and waving the line forward. Crates and barrels stack along the fence, and the yard smells of straw, diesel, and wet rope.

The party talks its way in behind the goods. The clerk checks manifests, not faces, and a wagon that holds up the line is everyone's problem, so he would sooner wave a doubtful one through than stop the war's supper arriving.

Depending on the hour of their plan, the yard offers different cover.

Skill Checks

Deception or Persuasion (Routine 13 with a forged requisition or work cover, Hard 19 on talk alone) to be waved through. - Success and they roll into the yard with the cargo, bound for the Loading Dock. - Failure +1 Doom and a second look; a second failure turns them out among the Crossing Camp or back to another way in.

Insight (Routine 13) to read the clerk. - Success and they see he cares about the line moving, not the law; leaning on that grants advantage. - Failure and they misread him and press the wrong point.

Sleight of Hand (Tricky 16) to lift a spare manifest or work chit. - Success and they pocket cover that grants advantage at the next gate. - Failure +1 Doom and the clerk catches the hand near his papers.

pages.name: Long Hallways
pages.html:
Long Hallways

Corridors. Day/Night. ~10-15 min

Long corridors run off under evenly spaced lamps, walls papered with notice boards and muster lists. Closed office doors line both sides, most of them locked. The floor is polished to a shine.

The Long Hallways connect the inner sections of the building. There is no gate to pass. The party moves through its corridors, reads the walls, and works toward the rooms it wants. Let the players choose between the mailroom, the mess, or the laundry.

The mood of anyone the players meets changes with the Doom Counter: low, a nod is enough; higher, personnel grow curious and want a badge; at the alarm, the halls turn to Assault Mode.

Skill Checks

Investigation (Routine 13) to read the notice boards. - Success, the shift schedule and the layout grant advantage on Stealth and Deception checks. - Failure, nothing useful.

Deception, Insight, or Stealth (DC by current Doom) to handle whoever crosses their path. - Success, continue to their destination. - Failure +1 Doom, this might escalate.

Random Encounter

Roll 2d6 each time the party enters the Long Hallways. Play the result at the corridors' current mood.

2d6 In the corridor
2-3 Nothing; the corridor is just the corridor.
4 A superior sweeps by with an entourage; high exposure.
5 Master Sergeant Temple corners a subordinate, eyeing bystanders.
6 A patrol turns in ahead; duck or bluff.
7 An officer stops them for a badge.
8 A runner asks them directions to a berth.
9 A talkative clerk latches on with gossip.
10-12 Nothing; the corridor is just the corridor.

pages.name: Mail Room
pages.html:
Mail Room

Mail Room. Day/Night. ~10-15 min

Pigeonholes climb every wall over a long sorting table heaped with letters, twine, and a canvas sack of post. A bank of brass pneumatic tubes lines one wall, canisters racked beside a board of labeled stations. A logbook lies open on a desk, and high on the far wall a duct grille hangs loose. The room smells of paper, ink, and sealing wax.

An easy room. The building's mail and internal messages pass through here, and so do its door codes. The party comes for the codes, the layout, the duct, and the tubes.

The grille high on the wall is a way through to the Maintenance Room. Any character with Passive Perception 12 clocks it as passable; no check.

  • Day. A clerk or two sorting; blend in or wait for a gap.
  • Night. Empty.
Skill Checks

Investigation (Routine 13) the open logbook and shelves. - Success: they lift the door codes and a facility map. The codes open the freight lift and the sealed-basement doors with no roll and no noise. - Failure and it takes time; +1 Doom if the party is pressed.

Perception (Tricky 16) the pigeonholes for anything out of place. - Success: a misrouted chit for the sealed basement, initialed by Colonel Standard. - Failure and it is only other people's mail.

Deception (Tricky 16, by the lie's plausibility) to send a false order by pneumatic tube. - Success: name a station; a post empties, a patrol redirects, or a room clears for a short window. - Failure +1 Doom, and someone wires back asking who sent it.

pages.name: Crossing Camp
pages.html:
Crossing Camp

Outside the Wire. Day/Night. ~10-15 min

Against the outside of the wire, the displaced have made a town of tarps and barrows. Cook-fires smoke, a child sleeps on a sack, a woman sells tea she has too little of. Everywhere people are packing: bundling belongings, trading for road food, roping barrows for the road north.

The camp presses against the delivery yard, people the siege pushed off the outer lands. During the daytime, the camp is busy with people doing things and it is an easy task to fit in. At night, the yard will have less people and they will be more observant. Stealth and deception are still options, but more difficult (disadvantage). Word is the army is moving, and two companies are preparing to follow.

Skill Checks

Stealth or Deception (Routine 13) to cross the camp unremarked. - Success and they reach the delivery yard without drawing eyes. - Failure and they leave a memorable impression a witness could describe later.

Persuasion or Deception (Routine 13) if the players are noticed and someone says something. - Success: the yard's rhythm (time the watch change for advantage going in). - Failure and they get only rumor and noise.

Perception or Insight (Routine 13) to pick up on the fact that some troops are getting ready to deploy. Advantage to those with a military background. - Success: Word the army moves north tomorrow, and a borrowed coat or barrow for cover. - Failure: No consequences.

pages.name: Laundry
pages.html:
Laundry

Yard Laundry. Day/Night. ~10-15 min

Great copper vats boil and churn, and the air hangs thick with steam and the smell of soap and hot cotton. Racks of drying uniforms stand in ranks, every trade and rank and size, pressed and waiting for the men they belong to. A drain grate sits in the corner of the wet tile floor.

The building's laundry, and the place to get a proper disguise. The racks hold the whole garrison's dress; the party comes for uniforms and gets in and out unseen. The grate in the corner is the inside end of the drainage pipe, the hidden way in.

Skill Checks

Group Stealth (night) or Group Deception (day) (Tricky 16) to take uniforms and get out unnoticed. - Success and they leave dressed as garrison staff, unremarked. - Failure and someone at the racks notices; +1 Doom .

Investigation (Routine 13) to pick the right dress for where they are going. - Success: uniforms that fit the destination, granting advantage on later Stealth and Deception while worn. - Failure and they grab a wrong rank or trade that draws a second look.

Rumors

The following Rumors can be overheard in any of the places soldiers congregate.

d6 Rumor
1 A whole unit shipped north this morning, quiet and early.
2 A company of regulars goes up tomorrow as reserves.
3 It is Pashendale. The Division is being fed into it.
4 The blockade is tighter than the brass admit; rations are short.
5 The coated men come and go and answer to no one.
6 Bay's lot volunteered a fortnight back and went downstairs. Gone since.

pages.name: Mess Hall
pages.html:
Mess Hall

Yard Mess. Day/Night. ~10-15 min

Long tables and benches run the length of the hall, a serving counter down one wall with a wall of tin trays stacked at its end. The floor is scuffed boards, the lamps low and yellow, and the air the faint smell of industrial cleaner, tobacco, and old coffee.

If the players arrive during the night, there will only be a handful of soldiers on break drinking coffee. There is a good likelyhood they will ignore the party if they act like they belong.

During the day, only the most egregious behavior will garner any notice. While the players are here, they have a chance to overhear some scuttlebutt.

Skill Checks

Persuasion (Routine 13) to get talking. - Success: roll or pick a rumor; a soldier warms to them, good for a vouch (advantage at the next checkpoint). - Failure +1 Doom, a wrong question draws further scrutiny.

Insight (Tricky 16) to sort truth from barracks embroidery. - Success: they can sort fact from fiction. - Failure: they cannot tell, and may chase a tall tale.

pages.name: Barracks
pages.html:
Barracks

Off-Watch Quarters. Day/Night. ~10-15 min

Rows of iron bunks with footlockers at their feet, wool blankets squared away, kit hung on pegs down the walls. A washstand stands at one end under a single low lamp. The air is boot polish, gun oil, and cold cigarette smoke.

By day, men move between duties here, cleaning kit and trading talk; the party passes as personnel, or draws questions if it dresses or speaks wrong. At night most bunks hold sleeping men, with a sleepless few murmuring at the lamp, and the trouble is crossing without waking anyone. If a skill check goes south the nearest cover is the door through to the Showers.

The sleepless will talk, the same public gossip as the mess and nothing of the program. Footlockers can be rifled, but the men keep letters and contraband there, not the lab's secrets.

Skill Checks

Deception (Tricky 16) by day, to pass among the men. - Success: through, and the sleepless share the north-movement gossip. - Failure +1 Doom, a soldier presses them.

Stealth (Tricky 16) by night, to cross without waking the room. - Success: through to the Mess or Showers unheard. - Failure: a sleeper stirs; duck into the Showers or +1 Doom.

pages.name: Duct Crawl
pages.html:
Duct Crawl

Ventilation Run. Day/Night. ~5 min

A steel crawlway barely wide enough for shoulders, warm from the boilers and thick with dust. Grilles below give onto the corridors it passes over. It runs level from the mail side to the maintenance side.

The crawl links the Mail Room and the Maintenance Room, past the corridor between them. It is a squeeze and a little noise, not a challenge. Narrate it through, unless the party rushes or the halls are quiet enough for sound to carry.

Skill Checks

Stealth or Athletics (Routine 13), only if they hurry or the halls are silent. - Success: through to Maintenance or the Mail Room unheard. - Failure +1 Doom, a clang at a grille turns a head below.

pages.name: Showers
pages.html:
Showers

Bath Block. Day/Night. ~10-15 min

White tile floor to ceiling, two rows of brass showerheads over a trough drain. Wire baskets and a bench line one wall, a duckboard walkway keeps feet off the wet, and a door leads through to the barracks. The air is carbolic soap and damp.

By day the room is full of men washing and larking, kit unguarded in the baskets. The party can lift a badge, a uniform, or a sidearm. A bad roll tips it to farce on the wet tile: loud, embarrassing, never deadly.

By night it is empty and wrong. Fog hangs where no water runs, and footsteps come back a beat late. Anyone found here off-hours is a spy, and the finder raises the alarm. Sleight of Hand (Tricky 16) by day, to lift a badge, uniform, or sidearm. Failure: caught reaching, farce, +1 Doom, no harm.

Stealth (Tricky 16) by night, to cross or search unheard. Failure: someone checks, and being found raises the alarm.

pages.name: Checkpoint
pages.html:
Checkpoint

Inner Gate. Day/Night. ~10-15 min

The corridor narrows to a barrier and a manned desk, a ledger and telephone on it, a keypad door beyond. A sign reads AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL ONLY.

The guard holds this gate, and getting past him is the scene. He checks papers, and the barrier answers to him. Nothing here gets picked or read while he watches; the party bluffs him, draws him off, or puts him down.

Prep pays. A cover or cleared name makes the bluff hold. A Maintenance power-cut or a false tube order calls him away, and the Mail Room code works the barrier before he returns. Putting him down is fast, loud, and soon noticed.

Skill Checks

Deception or Persuasion (Hard 19, Extreme 22 thin cover) to make the guard wave them through. Failure: +2 Doom, he does not budge.

Stealth (Tricky 16) to slip past while he is drawn off the desk. Failure: +1 Doom, he turns back too soon.

pages.name: Maintenance Room
pages.html:
Maintenance Room

Plant Room. Day/Night. ~10-15 min

Pipes and conduit run the walls to a board of gauges, valves, and switches that governs the heat, power, and water of the building. A duct opening in the corner is big enough to move through. A fitter's logbook hangs on a nail by the bench.

The controls here reach other rooms, and the party can spend them to ease the job. The duct runs to the Mail Room. The logbook is ordinary work orders, nothing of the program. By day a fitter may be at the bench; by night it is empty.

Read the board, throw a switch, and something happens where the party is going:

  • Lights: kill a corridor or a room for stealth, or to pull the checkpoint guard.
  • Steam: flood the Laundry or Showers for cover, or cut it to expose.
  • Freight lift: power the lift for a party without its code.
Skill Checks

Investigation (Tricky 16) to read the board and know which control hits which room. Failure: a wrong guess trips the wrong system.

Thieves' tools or tinkering (Tricky 16) to work a control. Failure: +1 Doom, an alarm sounds or the wrong room goes dark.

pages.name: Stairs Down
pages.html:
Stairs Down

Fire Stair. Day/Night. ~2 min

A fire stair turns down flight by flight, the noise of the building thinning at each landing. At the bottom a heavier door, cold air seeping under it, and a keypad beside the frame.

Beyond the Checkpoint, through a fire door, the players can find the stairs down to the Special Police Lab. If the alarm has been raised, the players will encounter a squad of special police ready to repel attackers.

At the bottom of the stairwell, the players encounter a locked door. The mailroom code opens it, or the players can attempt a Thieves' Tools or Athletics check to open it (Extreme 22).

pages.name: Loading Dock
pages.html:
Loading Dock

Cargo Dock. Day/Night. ~10-15 min

A concrete dock stacked with pallets and hand-trucks, a tally board on the wall, a raised lip along the cargo doors, and a side bay off one end. The air is diesel and packing straw.

During the day, players may attempt to move like they belong: Athletics to carry a load, Stealth to fit in with the dock crew, or Intimidation to bark orders (Routine 13).

During the night, Stealth to slip past any guard on duty (Tricky 16).

Any failure attracts scrutiny. +1 Doom.

Reading the tally board shows which routes run to the lower levels, pointing the party at Storage and the way down. A borrowed load or work chit passes as cover deeper in, and the side bay is a spot to catch a breath or change a coat.

pages.name: Storage
pages.html:
Storage

Bulk Stores. Day/Night. ~10-15 min

A cavern of shelving and crates, dim and cold, aisles running off into the dark. Down one end a whole section stands empty, clean rectangles in the dust where crates sat until recently, a clipboard hanging on a post beside the gap. A freight elevator sits flush in the floor by the south wall.

A store-man or a night guard is the only obstacle. Players get past on Stealth to slip the aisles, or Deception, Persuasion, or a charm to talk past (Tricky 16). Failure raises the alarm; if it sticks, jump Doom to the Assault Mode threshold.

The clipboard by the empty section is a manifest, readable by anyone who looks: the crates staged here shipped north to Pashendale this morning. This is the party's operational glimpse of the movement, matching the mess gossip and the Records roster.

The shelves hold useful stock: alchemical supplies, ammunition, rubbing alcohol, glass bottles, and bulk goods a clever party turns into tools. Taking it is a matter of what they carry.

The freight elevator on the south side goes down to the sealed basement.

pages.name: Elevator Down
pages.html:
Elevator Down

Freight Lift. Day/Night. ~5 min

An iron cage on a greased shaft, its gate concertinaed shut. The control panel has a keypad and a row of floor buttons, one below the numbered floors and unmarked. The cage is loud, and there is no making it quiet.

The way down to the sealed basement, twin to the stairs. With the Mail Room code, the party rides down, no check. Without it, they override the panel on Thieves' tools or tinkering (Hard 19), or climb the shaft ladder on Athletics (Tricky 16).

The lift is loud however they take it. Riding or overriding it at night risks a night-duty ear. +1 Doom.

pages.name: Main Lab
pages.html:
Main Lab

Sealed Basement. Day/Night. ~10-15 min

The lift opens on a laboratory the size of a drill hall: rows of benches and glassware, a centrifuge, racks of labeled reagents. Captured arms lie tagged and half-stripped on one bench, a technical drawing pinned above another, a medical shelf along the wall. A heavy coded door stands in the east wall.

By day, scientists work the benches under a Special Police minder, and the party must belong or bluff to move among them. By night it is empty and dark, free to search, the risk a night-duty minder or technician passing through.

Run it as a round-robin: around the table, each player picks one thing to examine or take, one check of their choosing. Reward curiosity. A fumble draws the minder by day or makes noise by night. +1 Doom.

Nothing of the Mythos is here. The dark work is behind the coded door, and the party should leave this room certain of that.

What they can work:

  • Captured Sous Terreborgue arms, an Infernal Rifle and Pistol, tagged and half-stripped.
  • A War Carriage drawing, pinned and annotated; readable intelligence, not ciphered.
  • The medical shelf: healing potions, potions of poison resistance, and two or three unlabeled.
  • Reagent racks (Arcana or Medicine): legitimate science, and the restricted work is elsewhere.
  • Duty paperwork, readable and pointedly not signed by Colonel Standard; it points at the coded door.

The coded door to the secured hallway wants its 3-digit code, from the Mail Room, a guard post, or Records. It is the way to the dark rooms, and the next objective.

pages.name: Records Room
pages.html:
Records Room

Sealed Basement. Day/Night. ~10-15 min

Filing cabinets wall to wall, a card index on a long table, packing crates half-filled by the door, and a stove in the corner burning low. Most of the paper is written in a hand no outsider can read. Some of it is not.

The program keeps its paper here, mid-sort: files pulled and packed in a hurry when the Division was ordered north. By day a clerk may be sorting; by night the room is empty. The ciphered mass is worth bagging but unreadable tonight. What the party can read now is the operational paper, and it hands them the two keys to the dark end.

  • A door-code sheet carrying the Sealed Lab 3-dial code and the secured-hallway code.
  • A room-assignment sheet: which of the three identical hallway doors is the Sealed Lab, the true-door tell.

  • A movement roster: the unit that shipped north this morning, headed by Sergeant Bay. This ties the Storage manifest and the mess gossip together.

  • Ciphered records. bag it and crack it over days.

  • Anatomical plate, a jackal-headed proportion study etched on brass.
Skill Checks

Investigation (Tricky 16) to work the card index and pull the three sheets fast. Failure: time lost in the wrong drawer, +1 Doom. Without the index the slow way still finds them, and costs a Doom tick.

History or a military background (Tricky 16) to read the roster in context and place Bay's unit as this morning's movement. Failure: the connection is missed for now.

Sleight of Hand (Hard 19) to salvage a half-burned page from the stove. Failure: it crumbles and the stove flares, +1 Doom.

Frame the subjects in the scraps as men who suffered, not monsters. This is the party's first real feel for what was done here.

Case-Note Scraps (d6)
d6 Scrap
1 "...the serum worked on him, pain and delusion rising, until he tore free of his restraints and both hands from his arms at the wrist..."
2 "...volunteered. Reason given: a brother lost over the wire. Cooperative through the third dose. After the fourth, no longer answers to his name..."
3 "...hearing and sight beyond any man's. He wept at the noise of the ward and asked, over and over, for it to stop..."
4 "...wounds close in hours. The trouble is not keeping him alive. It is the mind, which the body outlasts..."
5 "...Sgt. Bay passed final evaluation and went forward with the vanguard this morning. Steadiest on record. Asked only that the men who did not make it be sent home as fallen, not as failures..."
6 "...recommend the psychiatric officer stay with the movement. The ones that succeed are worse to manage than the ones that fail. They know what they are..."

pages.name: Morgue
pages.html:
Morgue

Secured Hallway. ~10-15 min

Cold air rolls out around your ankles, carbolic over something sweeter underneath. A wall of steel drawers faces you, most of them tagged, and in the middle of the floor a gurney waits with its sheet drawn up over a shape that is the wrong size for a man. One of the drawers, low on the left, is not quite closed.

These are the program's failures, the men it killed over weeks of trying, not the vanguard that went north this morning. They volunteered, and monstrous things were done to them; play them as soldiers who suffered, never as monsters. The bodies are the readable record here, and the checks draw it out. It ruins men differently each time, and there is something of the animal in how it fails. Describe that, and never explain it.

Skill Checks

Medicine (Tricky 16) to read a body: the serum meant to enhance instead kills, and these deaths span weeks. Failure: a wound misread, the party lingers, +1 Doom.

Investigation (Tricky 16) to follow the gurney tracks to the true Sealed Lab door among the three. Failure: the search disturbs the left drawer.

Survival or Nature (Tricky 16) to read the animal character, tying these dead to the subjects next door and the guard. Failure: nothing, an unsettling look.

Insight (Routine 13) to date the room's use: run steadily, used within the day, not abandoned. Failure: a wrong guess about the timeline.

Perception (Routine 13) to clock the not-quite-closed left drawer. Failure: it becomes a problem on its own.

The left drawer: its occupant is cold but not stiff, and shifts when disturbed. Atmospheric dread by default; it can rouse to seize a wrist or slide off its slab.

Remnant AC9, 1HP, triggers Mythos Check.

pages.name: Specimens
pages.html:
Specimens

Secured Hallway. ~10-15 min

A row of cells with iron-barred fronts, most of them dark. In the ones that are not, something moves. A man, or what was made from one, stands too still at the bars and follows you with eyes that are, terribly, still a man's. From the far cell a low whine breaks into a bark, then settles, like an injured animal looking for someone to stop the hurt.

The changed men who lived, earlier subjects, not the vanguard. This is the clearest look the party gets at what was done to Bay's men before they meet the guard. Every subject is injured, dangerous, and more experiment than human, and each was a soldier who volunteered to help the war and had monstrous things done to him. The aim is fear for Bay, not of him.

The far cell holds the lucid one. He answers with a single word, "Doctor," said differently every time: a question, a plea, a warning, a curse. Play the meaning through inflection. He cannot say more, and he knows it, which is worse. Provoking or freeing a subject is the danger.

Skill Checks

Medicine (Tricky 16) to examine a subject: the changes match the Morgue's dead, and predate this morning. Failure: it reacts to handling, +1 Doom.

Insight (Tricky 16) to read the lucid one: he volunteered, he is in pain, and he knows what he is. Failure: misread as an animal, the human read lost.

Investigation (Tricky 16) on the warden's log for how many subjects, and how long the program has run. Failure: a latch is disturbed.

Perception (Routine 13) to find the one cell not truly latched. Failure: it is found the hard way.

The unlatched cell. Provoke the room or miss the Perception, and a subject gets loose.

Abhorrent Soldier AC15, Durability 3, Regen +20, +12 to Hit, 3d8+4 Damage

Mythos exposure. A character who truly registers the lucid one makes a Wisdom save (lowest roll fails). The Dread Insight is the human cost, not the secret.

pages.name: Sealed Lab
pages.html:
Sealed Lab

Secured Hallway. ~15-20 min

The door gives onto a long white room that does not belong in a barracks. Steel tables stand in a row beneath caged lamps, their leather straps hanging open. A dictation machine has run its cylinder to the end and rides the dead groove, hissing. Against the far wall a big man in a soldier's undershirt turns his head toward the light, and rises.

One of the three identical hallway doors, opened by the code and the true-door tell from Records or the Morgue tracks. Standard and his Special Police went north this morning, and Pemberton with them, pressed in to manage the subjects, never in charge. What is left is the evidence, the strongbox, and the guard.

The guard is the boss: a soldier the program kept as a watchdog, not fit to send forward. Play him as a man who had monstrous things done to him, injured and dangerous and more experiment than man, and not a villain. He is what was done to Bay's people, still alive and set to guard a door. Putting him down should cost the party something.

The fight. The objective is the strongbox, not the kill; subduing, restraining, or slipping past all count. The key hangs at his neck, so downing or grappling him is the clean route. Use the room: the steel tables and straps pin him, the caged lamps break for dark, the dosing station is glass and chemicals. It is loud this deep, and if the alarm is not up, this raises it. Expect Assault Mode on the way out.

Abhorrent Rear Guard AC18, Durbility 8, Regen +20, Reach 10 ft., Epic Boss

The evidence. The strongbox on its trolley holds the evidence and the Pale Journal page. The key on the guard opens it, or force it (loud, +1 Doom), or work the 3-dial code if the party found it. All but the movement order is ciphered, carried out to crack over days. The readable seams are the dictation cylinders, Pemberton's clinical evaluations reporting upward, and the authorization sheets carrying Colonel Standard's name. The movement order pinned by the door names Pashendale.

Miss Constance Sharp

Rationalist journalist, thirty-four.

AC11; HP9; Hatpin+1/1d4; Investigation+5, Insight+5, Persuasion+3

Description: Plain dress, deliberate. Notebook in her hand. Sharp jaw, level gaze.

Mannerisms: Writes during conversations. Repeats a speaker's own words back at them as questions.

Intent: Wants to embarrass at least two people in this room and file the piece by Friday. Came to debunk.

Special Policeman

Humanoid, CR 5. Full kit in the Bestiary.

AC16; HP50; Truncheon+3/1d8+2; Service Revolver+4/1d8+2 (rech 5)

Description: A cold, competent officer of the Special Police in a good plain coat, badge unshown.

Mannerisms: Falls back without provoking opportunity attacks; throws itself flat to make an attack miss (Hit the Deck).

Intent: Take the target and the evidence, leave no witness to the cover-up. Endlessly replaceable.

pages.name: Horrors
pages.html:
Abhorrent Soldier

Medium Aberration, CR 8, see Bestiary. AC16; HP143; Claw+11/3d8+5 slash (rech 3); Wretched Bellow DC17 Con: 6d10+5 thunder + Deafened (rech 5); Locked Grip DC17 Str: Grappled + Restrained (rech 4); Serum-Wrought Flesh (resistance to non-silvered B/P/S); Standing Orders. Description: A soldier warped by super-soldier serum, larger than a man, thicker of skin, blunted of mind. No equipment. Hands are claws.

Mannerisms: Advances, closes, hits hard. Catches a missed swing and locks the attacker in place for the next Claw. Discipline cracks under 20+ damage from one hit; a name or fragment of a prayer bleeds through in one of a dozen voices.

Intent: A specimen restrained in a lab, released. Fights to hold ground because that is what training taught. Non-silvered weapons are resisted.

Abhorrent Rear Guard

Large Aberration, CR 10, see Bestiary. AC20; HP360; Wheel and Slam+12/4d8+7 bludg + push 10 ft. (rech 2); Chase Down+12/4d10+7 pierc + Grappled DC18 (rech 3); Flanking Bite+12/3d10+7 pierc + reposition (rech 4); Jackal's Howl DC17 Con: 8d10+7 thunder + Deafened + Prone (rech 5); Locked Jaws DC18 Str: Grappled + Restrained + drag 10 ft. (rech 4); Sundering Bite 6d8+7 pierc auto vs Grappled (rech 6); Epic Boss Resistance d20/11+ ends effect; Two Heads; Serum-Wrought Flesh. Description: A larger, later-generation Abhorrent. Two heads share the same shoulders: one Jackal, one Human. Four-limbed asymmetric bulk. Speaks in barks and half-words.

Mannerisms: Never stops moving. Every strike closes a gap or opens one. The Jackal head chases and bites; the Human head barks orders and locks grips. Howls at each HP threshold, blowing back everyone in earshot.

Intent: The line-holder. Punishes anything that moves past its position. The two heads act as separate Responses each round, doubling the pressure on the party.

pages.name: Overview
pages.html:
A Shadow in the Night

The Trooper reached Anchester a day ahead of the soldiers who carried home word of the victory. He is changed now, no longer a thinking man, and he is hunting the city for his wife. He does not know she is already gone. The Special Police cannot afford to have him found and questioned, so they have loosed Sergeant Aberdeen, the volunteer who did the real killing at Paschendale, to run him down. His kills and the Trooper's look the same. Bodies have begun to turn up across the wards. The party takes up the hunt, the Special Police a step behind them and Aberdeen a step ahead.

Episode Summary
Players 3–6, Level 7
Duration ~4 hours
Pacing Player-Led Investigation; Chase; Combat
Scenes 6 (4)
Cast Miss Sharp; Sir Stowe; the Special Police; five horrors
Reward A page of the Pale Journals; the Shadow's Journal; jars of stolen memory
References Doom Counter; Dread Insight; Chase System; Curse System; Mythos stat blocks; residential maps

Timeline

Fifteen years ago. A collector had the Pale Journals stolen from the Temple of Anhur in Sai Abbadon.

Two years ago. Zeshagu warriors joined Sous Terreborgue and took Sai Abbadon.

One year ago. Zeshagu's dragons and Sous Terreborgue's warships sealed Anchester. The collector had the Journals copied, and pages leaked into the city.

Six months ago. The Special Police secretly began building super-soldiers from something found in one of the stolen Journals.

Three months ago. Academics were found dead, skulls opened above the brow. The wards named the killer the Smiling Man.

Weeks ago. Drawn into the Clarion Society, the players hunted the Smiling Man eventually following him north to Paschendale.

Two days ago. At Paschendale the serum turned the volunteers, and they slaughtered the enemy, their allies, and one another. The players walked the field after.

Yesterday. A small caravan of regular infantry returned home and gave the city its victory: HEROES OF PASCHENDALE. One volunteer was not among them — a monstrous soldier AWOL and rushing home to his wife and unborn child.

Today. The Trooper is in Anchester, and a gruesome murder has occurred in a wealthy villa in North Ward. The Special Police hunt the one man who can unravel their lies. So do the players.

Episode Structure

This episode is a manhunt. The players are hunting the Trooper, gone AWOL from Paschendale and sneaking his way through Anchester. The players are racing the Special Police, who want him silenced. The players choose their path and the DM provides escalating scenes and conflict.

There are two new threats the players have not yet deduced: The Clairvoyant, a shadowy figure intent on finding the secrets to life and death within the pages of the Pale Journals, and Sergeant Aberdeen, the Volunteer who went mad during Paschendale and slew everyone before Dr. Pemberton and Colonel Standards were able to calm him.

The Clairvoyant desires the Unborn Child of the Trooper and has warned the Wife Claudia that the Special Police mean to do her harm through an anonomous tip to Claudia's friend. The two are on the run, hiding among the masses of people in a city that is filled with rubble and people trying to stay in-doors.

The Trooper is searching for her.

Aberdeen is searching for the Trooper.

The investigation culminates in a battle between the Trooper and Aberdeen where the players will be caught between two monstrous forces intent on killing each other. The Trooper dies in the end, and in a moment of final lucidity, begs the players to find his wife.

pages.name: How to Run the Crawl
pages.html:
Scene tags.

  • [SOCIAL/INFO] the party comes away with a lead that points them onward. Gossip, lore, and redundant facts do not count.
  • [COMBAT] a fight, only where the Trooper, Aberdeen, the Special Police, or a ward's own muscle is actually present.
  • Untagged is texture. Improvise, no prep.

The Doom Clock. Standard advancement. Each tier fires the next broadsheet handout and tightens the city. The finale is sprung when the Doom Clock reaches X (set this) or about two hours of table time have passed, whichever comes first. It is a trigger, not a place.

Getting closer is presentation. Leads run warmer, the murder handouts escalate, the clock visibly climbs. The content still just points onward. The tone tightens.

The three trails.

  • The women: Civic Archive to homes and workplace to Denman / Widow Ashe / pawn / coach to the hideout chain.
  • The murders: Bay flat to coroner to the killers.
  • The soldiers: coroner to Muster Office to Veterans' Fund to the Special Police.

Two killers, one signature. The Trooper and Aberdeen both leave the same monstrous kills. The players cannot tell them apart until late. The Trooper cannot pass among people; he moves cloaked, at night, through ruins and back ways, and only a sympathetic soul who knew him will risk speaking with him. He dens in empty places. The human nodes (homes, shops, offices, the university, lodging houses) hold the trail; the fights happen in the empty places.

pages.name: Drop-in Encounters
pages.html:
Use these when a scene turns to a fight. Drop into any ward.

SPECIAL POLICE (squad).

1 sergeant plus 2 to 4 officers.

SPECIAL POLICE SERGEANT. Humanoid, CR 6. AC16; HP68; Truncheon+4/1d8+3; Service Revolver+5/1d8+2 (rech 5). Cold Order (Response, rech 4): move 10 ft; one allied officer within 30 ft makes an immediate Revolver attack. Hit the Deck (Response, rech 3): move 5 ft; the next attack against the sergeant this round misses. Standing Orders: take the target and the evidence, leave no witness. Intent: detain the party, seize what they carry, be gone before the watch arrives.

SPECIAL POLICEMAN. Humanoid, CR 5. AC16; HP50; Truncheon+3/1d8+2; Service Revolver+4/1d8+2 (rech 5). Hit the Deck (Response, rech 5): move 5 ft; throw flat to make one attack miss. Endlessly replaceable. Intent: take the target and the evidence, leave no witness.

Reskin: same block in every ward. In Brasshold they arrive by launch; in Ash Ward they come with a warrant no one signed.

SERGEANT ABERDEEN (Epic Boss).

He does not fall in a ward scene. When the GM chooses, or when first bloodied, he breaks off and is gone, back on the Trooper's scent. His death belongs to the finale.

SERGEANT ABERDEEN, THE SECOND SURVIVOR. Unique Aberration (Epic Boss), CR 12. AC20; HP300. Acts after every PC's turn; on his own turn he only moves (up to 10 ft). Epic Boss Resistance: d20, 11+ ends an effect on him. Serum-Wrought Flesh: resistance to non-silvered bludgeoning, piercing, slashing. Rending Charge (Response, rech 2): move up to 10 ft; +12/4d8+7 slashing to one creature he reaches. Seize and Cast Aside (Response, rech 4): move 10 ft; DC18 Str or Grappled, then hurled 10 ft, Prone, 3d10 bludgeoning. Concussive Wrench (Response, rech 5): move 10 ft; DC17 Con, each creature within 10 ft takes 6d10 thunder, pushed 10 ft, Deafened. This is the "ripped apart by an explosion" the witnesses describe. Breaks Off: at the GM's call, or when first bloodied, Aberdeen disengages and leaves at full speed. He cannot be brought down in a ward scene. No Mercy: healing directed at him is answered with violence; at the finale it makes him seize and dissolve to goo. He cannot be saved. Intent: find the Trooper. Everything in the way is in the way.

Reskin: found scavenging a fresh kill, or forcing a door at a hideout.

DESPERATE LOOTERS.

Social first. A fight is easy; the point is whether the party makes it one.

DESPERATE LOOTERS (mob of 4 to 8). Medium Humanoids, CR 1/8 each. AC11; HP9; Club or Knife+2/1d6. Stand Down (social): DC13 Persuasion or Intimidation and they scatter; a fed or paid mob scatters at DC10. Broken Nerve: the first looter dropped or badly hurt, the rest test morale and most run.

LOOTER RINGLEADER. Humanoid, CR 1. AC12; HP22; Cudgel+3/1d8+1. Holds the mob together; if he falls or is talked down, the mob breaks. Intent: food, coin, and not to be the next name in the paper. Terror makes them stupid, not murderous.

Reskin: in East Row picking a shuttered shop; in Ash Ward a self-appointed watch that mistakes the party for the killer; on the docks a press-gang's leavings.

pages.name: The Finale
pages.html:
Sprung when the Doom Clock reaches X or about two hours of play, whichever comes first. It is not a place the players track down; it collapses onto them.

Where: a bombed-out church. Open to the sky, fallen roof beams and rubble, toppled columns and shattered pews for cover, a rubble ramp to a broken gallery, three ways in.

The fight: a three-way. The Trooper and Aberdeen arrive on each other, and the party is caught between them. The two monsters fight each other as much as the party. Aberdeen cannot be saved; every attempt to spare him ends the same way, and healing makes him seize and dissolve.

The intended end: the Trooper dies, and in a last moment of lucidity begs the players to find his wife. The wife is not here. She never was. (If the players find a way to save the Trooper, let them; a living Trooper is a witness who can unmake the victory, and the next episode carries that forward.)

Gargantuan Swarm of Medium Humanoids, CR 10. Full kit in the Bestiary.

AC18; HP180; Piling On+5/2d4+4; Rip and Drag DC16/4d6+4 (rech 5)

Description: A crowd of the hungry and the angry, hundreds strong, moving as one across a 20 by 20 space. Bricklayers, dockworkers, mothers with cast-iron pans, off-shift constables who did not come in today. Torches. Boots. Voices going hoarse.

Mannerisms: Pickpocket bonus action, DC 14 Dex or lose an item. Gives ground 15 ft. as a reaction when hit in melee, without provoking. Scatters when reaches half HP.

Intent: Take what they can while the city bleeds. Not enemies of the party. Very much in the way. Break them hard enough and they run.

Special Policeman

Humanoid, CR 5. Full kit in the Bestiary.

AC16; HP50; Truncheon+3/1d8+2; Service Revolver+4/1d8+2 (rech 5)

Description: A cold, competent officer of the Special Police in a good plain coat, badge unshown.

Mannerisms: Falls back without provoking opportunity attacks; throws itself flat to make an attack miss (Hit the Deck).

Intent: Take the target and the evidence, leave no witness to the cover-up. Endlessly replaceable.

Special Police Sergeant

Humanoid, CR 6. Full kit in the Bestiary.

AC13; HP54; Service Revolver+11/2d6+4; Baton Strike+11/1d10+4; Sweep the Line DC15/5d6+5 (rech 5)

Description: An older, harder officer of the Special Police. Half a dozen bad rooms behind him. His revolver is drawn before his men know they are in one.

Mannerisms: Barks orders as a bonus action, giving an ally advantage on the first attack against a designated target. Fires cover fire as a reaction when a hostile moves within 30 ft. of an ally. Allies within 30 ft. add +2 to attacks on their next turn.

Intent: Command the squad, secure the Trooper alive if the shot is clean, put him down if not. Every Policeman lost is a witness pruned.

Corporal Aberdeen

Epic Boss. Aberration, CR 12. Full kit in the Bestiary.

AC20; HP330; Rending Claws+14/5d10+4; Marrow Bite+15/10d10+7+Grappled DC18 (rech 5); Sergeant's Name DC17/6d8 psychic (rech 4); Regen 30/round

Description: Once a friend to Sergeant Bay. When Bay came back from the serum wearing a jackal's head, Aberdeen volunteered next. He came back as this. Twenty percent smaller than Bay. Twice as fast. All jealousy.

Mannerisms: Chases as a bonus action, 10 ft. toward whoever last damaged him or spoke Bay's name. Absorbs the hit as a reaction, shifting 10 ft. and reducing incoming damage by 15; if the damage is thereby reduced to 0, he regains 10 HP. Anyone who speaks Bay's name or heals another creature within 60 ft. draws his next attack with advantage.

Intent: Kill Bay. Everyone else in the room is between him and Bay, and will be treated accordingly. He will not stop.

Sergeant Bay

Epic Boss. Aberration, CR 12. Full kit in the Bestiary.

AC20; HP330; Cleaving Talon+14/5d10+4; Break the Line+15/10d10+7+push 15+Prone (rech 5); The Bride's Name DC17/6d8 psychic in 15 ft. (rech 4); Regen 50/round

Description: The decorated soldier who volunteered for the program. Recognizable, still, if you knew him. The serum kept the soldier and threw away the man. He is looking for his wife. He has not blinked in an hour.

Mannerisms: Rushes forward as a bonus action, 20 ft. in a straight line through creatures' spaces, provoking opportunity attacks. Follows a fleeing creature as a reaction, 10 ft. to stay adjacent, provoking opportunity attacks. Bypasses anyone who yields ground. Destroys anyone who does not. Cannot be slowed or held; regains 50 HP at the start of every round he did not end on 0 HP.

Intent: Find Claudia. Nothing else matters. If the party is between Bay and where he thinks she is, the party is scenery in the way of a hurricane.
